title: Anti-Corruption Layer

validation.research: Four primary sources: Eric Evans’s DDD Reference, Anticorruption Layer (printed page 34, PDF page 41); Microsoft Azure Architecture Center; AWS Prescriptive Guidance; and Martin Fowler’s Bounded Context article. The source PDF’s original summary was read. The article explains protection of a downstream model through locally expressed capability, requests, results, and failures. It distinguishes the original Anticorruption spelling and ACL shorthand from security access-control lists, model protection from mechanical adaptation, and permanent boundaries from temporary migration support. The primary home is Messaging and Integration; model and architecture overlaps are related links.

example_limits: Original sequential supplier-stock read simulation. The protected domain.py imports only standard-library definitions and owns frozen Availability, local StockUnavailable, and the positive-integer can_supply rule. boundary.py depends on that model, maps SKU-42 to ITEM-9, and validates an exact six-field decoded supplier version-1 record. A means active record, not available for sale. Total quantity includes disjoint committed and damaged categories from one coherent snapshot, so 10 minus 7 minus 2 yields 1 sellable unit. Unknown mapping stops before transport; malformed, unsupported, mismatched, or inconsistent records cannot create a local stock fact. TimeoutError is normalized to StockUnavailable with its cause; other unexpected errors are not broadly hidden. Caller mapping is copied; input response is not mutated. True zero stock is a known Availability and differs from unknown evidence. No network, stock mutation, atomic reservation, cache/freshness protocol, synchronization, authorization, client lifecycle, mapping updates, or automatic retry. The stub and arithmetic contract are teaching material, not a vendor or stock-allocation implementation.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
